ideas.title: Pintu-pintu yang beneran kebuka: hinge-accurate door swing + doorway-to-scene match cut
ideas.what:
Babak 1 jadi satu ruangan full-bleed, bukan list tombol. Satu SVG kamar subuh, 4 kaca pintu berdiri sejajar. Tiap pintu = 3 layer: (a) `doorway` rect = clip-path buat dunia di dalemnya, (b) `world` group yang digambar DI BELAKANG panel dan ke-clip ke doorway, (c) `panel` yang di-rotate.

Mekanik swing-nya: panel pakai `transform-origin` di sisi hinge-nya (pintu 1 & 2 hinge kiri, 3 & 4 hinge kanan — biar kaya koridor), parent-nya `perspective:620px`. Idle state pintu udah NGINTIP: `rotateY(-26deg)` + breathing loop `±3.5deg / 4.2s` dengan stagger 0.5s per pintu, jadi cahaya yang keluar ikut kedip-kedip (`<rect>` warm light opacity 0.35↔0.6 di-sync delay-nya sama). Jadi sebelum disentuh pun ruangan ini udah hidup.

Pas di-tap: panel ayun ke `rotateY(-88deg)` 420ms `cubic-bezier(.3,1,.3,1)`, 3 pintu lain `translateX(±40px) scale(.9) opacity(.12)` 300ms, TERUS doorway-nya jadi frame scene berikutnya — animate clip rect dari ukuran pintu (misal 62×118) ke full viewport pakai satu `scale`+`translate` di clip group, 560ms `cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)`. Dunia di dalem pintu barengan `scale(1.25→1)`, jadi berasa kita JALAN MASUK, bukan ganti halaman. Zero white flash, zero cut.

Isi tiap pintu (sedikit suasana, pake art yang udah ada tinggal dipotong): Sorot = siluet kerumunan + 3 sorot lampu nyilang; Karya = meja penuh bunga/kain + tangan; Hati = koridor + satu siluet nungguin; Jelajah = jalan setapak + bukit + burung.
ideas.why: Ini satu-satunya momen di kuis ini yang bisa bikin orang bilang "eh apaan nih" di 2 detik pertama. Match cut doorway→scene juga sekalian NGEBUNUH masalah "journeynya patah": transisi pertama bukan fade, tapi perpindahan ruang yang bisa dilacak mata. Dan ini mustahil keluar dari AI generik — mereka bakal kasih 4 card dengan hover scale.

ideas.title: Suara tiap pintu, disintesis full WebAudio — nol file eksternal
ideas.what:
Satu `AudioContext` di-unlock di tap "Gas, mulai" (wajib buat iOS). 4 bed ambience, semuanya di-generate, jadi file tetep self-contained:

• **Sorot** — pink noise → bandpass 520Hz Q=0.8, LFO 0.08Hz di gain (0.04↔0.12) = kerumunan jauh. Plus grain tepuk tangan: 8 noise burst 30ms random tiap 2–4s lewat highpass 2kHz.
• **Karya** — room hum sine 92Hz gain .03, plus pola gunting/ketuk: noise burst 18ms → highpass 3.5kHz, pattern [0, 340, 520, 1100]ms looping 1.4s.
• **Hati** — 3 ketukan pintu: noise 45ms → lowpass 320Hz, decay exponential, jeda 280ms, ulang tiap 6s. Di bawahnya detak jantung: dua sine 58Hz, 90ms, jeda 180ms, tiap 1.1s.
• **Jelajah** — brown noise → lowpass yang di-sweep 300↔900Hz pakai LFO 0.05Hz = angin. Plus 2 chirp burung: sine glide 2.1k→2.8kHz dalam 70ms, random tiap 5–9s.

Koreografi "nyapa": pas screen pintu muncul, keempat bed jalan tapi gain 0.0; terus sequence 2.2s per pintu — gain naik ke penuh + cahaya pintunya ikut brighten + panel-nya ngayun lebih lebar 6deg. Keempat pintu "ngomong" satu-satu, baru semuanya turun ke gain 0.25 (ambient mix) dan nunggu dipilih. Pas di-tap: pintu kepilih gain ke 1.0 sambil 3 lainnya fade 400ms ke 0 — audio-nya ikutan "masuk" bareng visualnya.

Plus sound grammar buat sisanya: tap opsi = sine 660Hz 60ms (tiap opsi beda interval, pentatonic, jadi nggak bosen), takeout muncul = soft marimba 880Hz, bar progress naik = tick 1.2kHz 25ms. Toggle 🔊/🔇 pojok kanan atas, state di `localStorage`, default ON tapi gain di-ramp 600ms biar nggak ngagetin.
ideas.why: Diminta eksplisit ("masing-masing ada suara") dan 90% implementasi lain bakal nyerah di sini karena mikirnya butuh mp3. Disintesis = tetep satu file, tetep offline, dan beda tiap pintu secara karakter bukan cuma beda pitch. Suara juga yang bikin "suasana" kerasa padahal gambarnya tetep SVG pastel sederhana.

ideas.title: Satu dunia yang jalan, bukan 10 gambar beda — garis horizon konsisten + jam matahari
ideas.what:
Semua scene udah pake viewBox `320×170` dan tanah di `y=132`. Manfaatin itu: hentikan swap `innerHTML` per pertanyaan, ganti jadi satu world layer permanen dengan 3 slot — `sky`, `ground`, `props`.

Transisi antar beat: (1) `--sky-a`/`--sky-b` custom property di-transition 700ms (pake `@property` biar gradient-nya bener-bener nge-tween, bukan nge-jump); (2) ground `translateX(-18px)` lalu balik ke 0 dengan `cubic-bezier(.33,1,.68,1)` = sensasi melangkah; (3) props lama turun ke bawah horizon `translateY(26px) opacity 0` 220ms, props baru naik dari bawah horizon dengan stagger 80ms per elemen. Jadi dunia nggak pernah ke-cut — dia JALAN.

Di atasnya: satu variabel `--sun` 0→1 jalan sepanjang 10 beat, nge-drive 4 hal sekaligus — stop gradient langit (subuh #FFEAD9 → siang #CFE9FF → senja #FFC9A8 → malam #CDBEF2), `--shadow-angle` buat semua drop-shadow (pagi panjang ke kanan, siang pendek, senja panjang ke kiri), suhu warna lewat `filter:sepia()` tipis 0→6%, dan density bintang. Progress bar lama bisa diganti/ditemenin matahari kecil yang naik-turun di busur — orang jadi tau posisinya di cerita tanpa baca "4/10".

Bonus murah: tiap jawaban nambahin satu prop permanen kecil di pinggir frame (kamera, bunga, pita) yang KEBAWA ke scene berikutnya. Di beat 10 pinggiran frame-nya udah penuh jejak pilihan dia sendiri.
ideas.why: Ini obat langsung buat "journeynya patah banget". Yang bikin patah bukan cuma narasinya — tiap pertanyaan sekarang literally ganti gambar dan ganti warna background secara mendadak. Horizon yang nyambung + matahari yang gerak bikin 10 beat kebaca sebagai SATU HARI. Dan jejak prop yang numpuk bikin orang ngerasa dunianya inget pilihan dia.

ideas.title: Jawaban tanpa teks: tile ilustrasi yang punya kata kerja sendiri
ideas.what:
Opsi jadi grid 2×2 tile 1:1 (di HP 2 kolom, tile ~150px — jauh di atas target 44px). Isinya mini-diorama SVG, nol teks, pake palet scene-nya.

3 lapis motion per tile:
1. **Idle** — tiap tile punya micro-loop unik biar grid-nya nggak mati: tile kamera lampu merahnya kedip tiap 2.4s; tile bunga satu kelopaknya jatuh pelan tiap 5s; tile panggung sorotnya nyapu kiri-kanan 3s; tile peta ada garis putus-putus yang "jalan" (`stroke-dashoffset` animasi). Stagger beda-beda biar nggak sinkron (sinkron = berasa robot).
2. **Press** — `scale(.94)` 90ms, terus tile-nya MELAKUKAN kata kerjanya sekali: shutter kamera nutup-buka, gunting ngatup, tangan ngelambai, kaki melangkah. 260ms, baru commit. Jadi tap-nya kerasa "kejadian", bukan cuma "kepilih".
3. **Commit** — 3 tile lain `opacity .14 scale(.88)` + grayscale 400ms, tile kepilih `scale(1.06)` terus FLIP ke posisi takeout card (baca rect-nya pakai `getBoundingClientRect`, animate ke slot tujuan, 520ms spring). Jadi kartu takeout-nya seolah TUMBUH dari jawaban yang dipilih.

Aksesibilitas & review: `aria-label` bawa teks yang dibuang visualnya, plus toggle "Aa" di header yang nampilin caption di bawah tile (kepake banget buat tim brand yang mau review copy, dan buat user yang bingung).
ideas.why: Diminta eksplisit ("lebih banyak image jangan terlalu banyak text"), tapi ilustrasi diem itu riskan — ambigu. Micro-loop idle yang bikin tile kebaca maksudnya tanpa caption, dan verb-on-press yang bikin tap-nya terasa fisik. FLIP tile→takeout juga ngilangin satu "patah" lagi: modal yang nongol dari mana-mana diganti kartu yang kelihatan asal-usulnya.

ideas.title: Reveal akhir: filmstrip 10 pilihan collapse jadi cermin
ideas.what:
Ganti loading screen 2.65s yang sekarang (mascot lompat-lompat + 3 dot) dengan sequence yang BAHANNYA punya user sendiri.

Sepanjang kuis, tiap tile kepilih nyisa jadi thumbnail 34px di filmstrip atas (strip-nya geser satu notch ke kiri tiap beat, pakai spring overshoot 4%). Di beat 10 ada 10 thumbnail = hari dia, kelihatan utuh.

Reveal, total ~3.4s, bisa di-skip dengan tap:
1. **0–0.6s** FLIP semua 10 thumbnail dari posisi strip ke tengah layar, stagger 26ms, easing `cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)` — berasa kaya semua pilihan ngumpul.
2. **0.6–1.0s** cluster-nya mengecil jadi satu titik terang sambil rotate 12deg; satu flash putih `opacity 0→.85→0` 180ms. Flash ini sekalian nyembunyiin DOM swap — jadi nggak akan pernah keliatan jump.
3. **1.0–1.7s** titik itu mekar jadi cermin: SVG ellipse clip, `ry` 0→penuh 620ms, mascot di dalemnya `scale(1.3→1)` (parallax kedalaman). Confetti yang udah ada di-retime ke sini, bukan ke `show('result')`.
4. **1.7–2.4s** nickname masuk per-huruf dari `translateY(18px) rotate(-8deg) blur(6px)` → 0, jeda 34ms. Audio: arpeggio naik C5–E5–G5 sine 120ms apart + shimmer (noise lewat bandpass 6kHz, fade 500ms).
5. **2.4–3.4s** bar trait ngisi satu-satu, stagger 90ms, knob-nya overshoot 6% baru settle. Satu haptic tick per bar mendarat — jadi hasilnya kayak "dibacain" ke badan.

Di sepanjang step 1–3, tahan copy-nya: satu baris aja, "Senja turun. Hari ini udah nulis sesuatu…" Jangan 4 baris rotating kaya sekarang.
ideas.why: Reveal itu momen yang di-screenshot dan di-share — ROI motion paling tinggi per baris kode. Dan bedanya sama versi AI generik: loading-nya bukan spinner palsu yang nungguin timer, tapi 10 pilihan user sendiri yang keliatan nyatu jadi satu jawaban. Secara naratif itu yang bikin hasilnya kerasa PANTES, bukan random.

ideas.title: Tata bahasa haptic — plus fallback buat iOS Safari yang nggak punya vibrate
ideas.what:
Bikin `haptic(name)` satu fungsi, satu kamus, dipanggil dari semua interaksi. Kuncinya: tiap event punya tekstur beda, jadi badan belajar artinya.

• tap tile = `12` (ketukan ringan)
• pintu kebuka = `[18,40,26]` (thunk-thunk, kaya daun pintu kena kusen)
• takeout nongol = `8`
• beat 5 (setengah jalan) = `[10,30,10]`
• bar trait mendarat = `6` ×4
• reveal = `[26,50,18,50,40]` (crescendo)
• invalid/locked = `[6,60,6]`

Masalahnya iOS Safari nggak support `navigator.vibrate` — jadi deteksi sekali, dan kalau nggak ada, jalanin **visual haptic** yang di-tune per-nama: `.stage` dapet `scale(.985)` 90ms dengan easing balik `cubic-bezier(.3,1.6,.5,1)`, dan buat event berat tambahin `filter:blur(.6px)` 60ms + satu ring pulse dari titik sentuh (`box-shadow 0 0 0 0 → 0 0 0 14px` fade out). Mata nangkep impact-nya walau kulit nggak. Honor `prefers-reduced-motion` di sini: bentuknya jadi flash opacity doang.
ideas.why: Di HP, haptic itu 40% dari kesan "mahal" dan hampir selalu dilupain. Yang bikin beda bukan ada-nya vibrate, tapi vibrate-nya BEDA-BEDA — pintu kerasa kayak pintu, tap kerasa kayak tap. Fallback visual juga penting karena setengah audiens Gen Z Indonesia pakai iPhone dan tanpa itu mereka dapet versi yang mati separo.

ideas.title: Koridor yang bisa diseret + kebijakan reduced-motion yang nggak membunuh cerita
ideas.what:
**Dua hal, dua-duanya pendek.**

(a) **Drag parallax di screen pintu.** Satu jari geser horizontal nggerakin koridor: kusen pintu (near) 1:1, dunia di dalem pintu (far) 1:0.6, lantai + doodle belakang 1:0.3. Momentum sederhana (`v *= 0.93` per frame) terus snap ke pintu terdekat pakai spring. Rubber-band di ujung: di luar batas, `translateX *= 0.35`. Satu pintu selalu agak lebih gede + lebih terang (focus state), dan ambience-nya yang paling kedengeran — jadi geser = "ngintip" pintu lain. Ini sekalian ngajarin gesture di awal, dan bikin 4 pintu kebaca sebagai TEMPAT bukan 4 tombol.

(b) **Ganti baris 290.** Sekarang `@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){*{animation:none!important;transition:none!important}}` — itu matiin juga animasi yang BAWA MAKNA (bar trait, progress, pintu kebuka), jadi user reduced-motion dapet pengalaman yang rusak, bukan yang tenang. Ganti jadi kebijakan berlapis: buang parallax, float, bob, breathing, shake, confetti; PERTAHANKAN semua crossfade opacity, pengisian bar, dan progress; pintu kebuka jadi crossfade 200ms antara art tertutup↔terbuka (maknanya tetep ada, geraknya nggak).

**Budget performa** biar mid-range Android tetep 60fps: cuma `transform`/`opacity` yang dianimasi, `will-change` CUMA di 2 layer yang gerak (jangan ditabur), confetti di-cap 70 partikel dan `devicePixelRatio` di-clamp ke 2, semua idle loop digate `.is-active` lewat satu `IntersectionObserver` jadi scene off-screen berhenti ngitung, dan `AudioContext.suspend()` pas `visibilitychange` hidden.
ideas.why: Drag bikin Babak 1 naik dari "4 pilihan cantik" jadi ruang yang bisa dijelajahi — dan itu persis janji "Made to Explore". Bagian (b) kelihatan kayak kerjaan belakang tapi tanpa itu semua ide di atas bisa jadi stutter di HP 2 juta, dan user reduced-motion dapet kuis yang setengah mati. Dua-duanya murah dan ngelindungin investasi di 6 ide sebelumnya.

ideas.title: Babak 1: empat pintu, empat cahaya — satu ruangan
ideas.what:
One portrait SVG (viewBox 340x420) of a dim pre-dawn room: wall #CDBEF2, floor #B9A8E6, with a 2x2 grid of arched doorways (rect + half-circle top, ~150x180, at x=14/176, y=16/212). Each door's inner panel is clipped and holds a 3-element diorama, not an icon: SOROT — bg #8E7FC6, a gold shaft from the top, five crowd dots in #6E5FA8, one mic silhouette. KARYA — bg #FFE3CF, a worktable edge, scissors + one flower + a fabric roll. HATI — bg #D8F5EE, two small round figures, one paw reaching out. JELAJAH — bg #DCEEFF, two converging path lines to a horizon, two hills, one bird chevron.

The move that sells it: light spills OUT of every door onto the shared floor. Four trapezoid paths from each threshold, filled in that door's own hue (#FFD36E / #FFB184 / #86E3C6 / #8FD0FF) at opacity .30–.34, each pulsing .24→.40 on its own 2.4–3.0s offset. Four flat rectangles become four worlds in one room, for about 12 lines of markup.

'Masing-masing ada suara' rendered as visible sound, CSS keyframes on SVG children so there is no per-frame JS: Sorot = 3-bar equaliser scaling on y; Karya = scissor blades rotating ±12° plus three paper flecks drifting; Hati = two concentric knock ripples (circle scale .6→1.4, opacity 1→0); Jelajah = three wind lines translating on x with staggered delays. Add one WebAudio sting per door on tap — a single OscillatorNode, 180ms ADSR, Sorot 880Hz saw / Karya 1320Hz pluck / Hati 523Hz sine / Jelajah 659Hz triangle. No files, fires only on a user gesture so nothing is autoplay-blocked, with a small mute toggle in the brandbar.

On tap, the chosen panel's rect scales from its own bounds to full-frame over 420ms while the other three fade to opacity .22 and take filter:saturate(.3); the Babak 2 scene then cross-fades in from that same colour. The door you chose literally becomes the next world. Narration stays as one line of copy under the art, never inside it.
ideas.why: It is the explicit headline request and the first real screen anyone sees, so it decides whether this reads as art-directed or auto-generated. Four doors drawn as four flat panels would be inert; the spilled light on a shared floor is what makes them feel like four atmospheres you could walk into, and the animated sound cues deliver 'ada suara' even on a muted phone. It also hands you a free, gorgeous Babak 1 → Babak 2 transition (the chosen hue flooding the frame), which is exactly where the journey currently snaps.

ideas.title: Jam Matahari — one dawn-to-dusk ramp driving the whole page
ideas.what:
Replace the ten unrelated scene hexes with an ordered HOURS array of 10 entries, each {skyTop, skyBot, light, shadow, accent, ground}. Suggested ramp: 05:30 #F6EEFF→#FFE8F0 (doors, pre-dawn violet with a warm crack of light under each door) · 07:00 #FFEAD9→#FFF6E6, accent #FFCE57 · 09:30 #FFF7E0→#FFFCF2 · 12:00 #EAF4FF→#FFFFFF (highest value, lowest saturation) · 15:00 #FFF3CE→#FFE8D4 · 17:00 #FFD9BE→#FFC6A8 (warmest, most saturated) · 18:30 #FFC2C9→#E4B8E8 · 19:30 #C9B9EE→#A99BDC · 20:30 #8E7FC6 with gold #FFF0B8 spotlight (lowest value, highest contrast — the climax) · 21:30 #6E5FA8→#CDBEF2 lifting at the horizon.

The curve is the point: value climbs to a bright, low-saturation midday, then descends so the gold spotlight at Babak 5 is the brightest pixel in the entire quiz, and the night resolution sits just above it. JS writes the active hour to :root as --sky-top / --sky-bot / --hr-light / --hr-shadow / --hr-accent / --hr-ground; body transitions background-color over 900ms; SCENES stop hard-coding fills and reference the vars instead.

Two supporting moves. The progress bar becomes a sun track: a 14px dot travelling the bar, #FFCE57 through the first six hours, morphing into a #FFF0B8 crescent (two overlapping circles, the upper one filled with the current sky colour) from hour seven, with the bar gradient sampled from the current and next hour — the progress indicator IS the time of day. And the scene frame loses its hard edge: the bottom 20px of the scene SVG carries the same gradient as the page beneath it, so the illustration sits in the page rather than on a card floating over it.
ideas.why: This is the 'color storytelling from dawn to dusk' the brief asks for, and it is the cheapest cohesion device available because it touches every screen at once. Right now the ten backgrounds read as a random pastel sampler, so there is no felt passage of time — which is a large part of why the journey feels patah. Tie page, scene, progress bar and share card to one ramp and the user feels the day moving without reading a single word of copy.

ideas.title: Jawaban jadi stiker — answer illustrations in a 2x2 grid
ideas.what:
Kill the `.opt` text row (46px emoji box + a full sentence) and replace it with a 2x2 grid of square tiles: aspect-ratio 1, border-radius 22px, background rgba(255,255,255,.9) over the hour tint, 2.5px solid transparent border. Inside each: a 76x76 inline SVG illustration plus a 2–3 word label at 12.5px/600 underneath. The illustration carries the meaning, the label is the safety net — going fully text-free is one CSS line away if you want to A/B it.

The discipline that keeps 30+ small drawings one family: 64x64 viewBox; max 3 fills (hour tint, white, hour accent) plus ink #43282A only for a face or a 2.5px line; no stroke thinner than 2.5px; every corner radius ≥3; at most one spark() per tile; the subject fills ~70% of the box, sits on an implied baseline at y=54, and gets a shadow ellipse. Critically, the tiles inherit the HOUR ACCENT rather than a global pink — Babak 1's four tiles are door-coloured, the stage scene's are gold. The answers change clothes as the day moves.

Select state: border takes the hour accent, tile lifts translateY(-3px) scale(1.03), illustration scales 1.08, a 20px heart badge pops bottom-right in the accent, the other three drop to opacity .5. Hold 300ms so the pick registers, then wipe.
ideas.why: The explicit ask — more image, far less text, an illustration per answer. It also fixes a concrete layout problem: four 64px text rows eat roughly 300px of phone height and shove the scene art above the fold, while a 2x2 tile grid lands near 230px and lets the scene illustration be about 40% bigger. Emoji-in-a-rounded-box is exactly what a generic build produces; hand-drawn tiles that recolour with the scene are what a brand produces, and they become free assets for the result filmstrip later.

ideas.title: Barang yang kebawa + transisi wipe senja
ideas.what:
Give every option a `carry` field: a small SVG snippet plus an anchor name. Define fixed anchors in the mascot's 220x236 space — neck (110,138), hand-L (58,160), hand-R (162,160), back (110,150), head (110,46) — and let mascotBase accept carry:[{anchor,svg}], rendering each at the scene's mascot scale. Cap at three visible, newest wins. Props: camera on a strap (neck), bouquet (hand-R), sketchbook (hand-L), stage-pass lanyard (neck), compass (hand-L), tote with a plant (hand-R), tiny crown (head). Pick the camera in Babak 1 and it is still hanging on her in Babak 5.

Pair it with one transition used everywhere: a fixed-position #wipe div filled with linear-gradient(var(--next-sky-top), var(--next-sky-bot)) and border-radius 50% 50% 0 0 / 22% 22% 0 0, animating translateY 110% → -10% over 380ms ease-in, swapping the scene at 55% and continuing off the top. Same curve, same duration, every time, so it becomes the quiz's rhythm. Note for implementation: carried props need per-render unique clipPath/gradient ids or Safari will reuse the wrong clip.
ideas.why: This is the visual answer to 'journeynya patah banget'. Rewriting copy helps, but the image is what proves continuity — seeing the camera you chose at dawn still around her neck at dusk is proof the story remembered you, and almost nothing auto-generated bothers to do it. The wipe in the NEXT hour's sky colour means every transition reads as time passing rather than a page swapping, which stitches the ten beats into one continuous day.

ideas.title: Satu panggung, satu horizon — the scene composition grid
ideas.what:
Rebuild SCENES against a locked stage instead of composing each one ad hoc. viewBox goes 320x210 (up from 170) with rx 26, so there is room for a foreground plane. Horizon locked at y=118 in all ten scenes — sky above as the hour gradient, ground below in the hour's ground colour with a 10px lighter band right at the horizon line. Mascot feet always land at y=182, and only three scales are legal: near 92, mid 68, far 48 (replacing today's arbitrary 50–70 at y 54–88).

Hard caps: ONE hero prop at 40–70% of frame height, at most two secondary props. The current scenes carry six to eight objects at similar sizes, which is precisely why they read busy and flat. Add exactly one cropped foreground element per scene at opacity .5–.6, bleeding off the left or right edge — a leaf cluster, a curtain fold, a railing, a vase lip, a blurred string of lights. That single addition is the biggest amateur-to-art-directed lever available, because it creates three depth planes instead of one.

Light comes from the upper right in every scene (consistent with the sun's path in the ramp), so add one shared helper sh(x,y,rx) dropping a #43282A opacity .07 ellipse offset down-left under every object. Compose the hero prop and the mascot on opposite thirds (x≈96 and x≈224), never both centred.
ideas.why: Beauty and cohesion here are mostly geometry, not more detail. A locked horizon, three mascot scales, one foreground plane and one light direction turn ten unrelated vignettes into ten frames of a single film, and it costs nothing at runtime. It also leaves whoever adds scene eleven a rule to follow instead of a guess, so the system does not drift the moment the campaign extends.

ideas.title: Maskot jadi aktor — poses and a swappable face layer
ideas.what:
Refactor mascotBase(halo, topper, prop) into mascotBase({pose, face, topper, prop, carry, halo}).

Poses, swapping body paths only: `stand` (current), `reach` (right arm up, body tilted 4° — the doors, the spotlight), `lean` (whole group rotated 6°, one foot forward — curiosity, the expo), `sit` (legs tucked, body rect 10px shorter, feet ellipses dropped — cozy and free-time beats), `jump` (both arms up, feet lifted 12px, shadow ellipse rx reduced 30% and opacity raised 50% so the lift actually reads).

Faces, swapping only the eye/mouth/cheek group: `calm` (current), `wow` (eyes become two 7px spark() shapes, mouth a filled o), `blush` (eyes as closed arcs M-6 0 Q0 -6 6 0, cheek rx up to 12), `soft` (half-lid rects over the eyes), `nervous` (one eyebrow line, mouth a flat 10px line, one drop()).

Each scene then names a state, so the emotional arc is authored rather than accidental: curious at the doors → excited in the crowd → melting at the compliment → nervous when things fall apart → wide-eyed in the spotlight → content under the night sky. And on answer tap, swap to a 300ms reaction face before the wipe fires, so she responds to what you picked.
ideas.why: The mascot is already the strongest brand asset in this file, but it holds one pose and one face across every screen, so it functions as a sticker pasted onto scenes rather than as the person living this day. Five poses times five faces is roughly 40 lines of path data and buys 25 readable emotional beats. A character whose expression tracks the story is the line between 'cute mascot' and 'illustrated narrative', and it is the exact kind of patient detail a generic generator skips.

ideas.title: Hasil: aura arketipe + filmstrip harimu
ideas.what:
Hero card background becomes a radial aura from the archetype's c1 to c2 laid over the hour-10 night sky, with 20 sparkles whose positions are seeded from the archetype key (a tiny LCG over charCodes) so the same archetype always produces the identical layout. Determinism matters here: a shareable card should look like a designed poster, not a fresh random render each time.

Under the hero, add a filmstrip — ten 44x44 chips, each showing the 64x64 illustration of the answer YOU picked, tinted in that question's hour colour, laid left to right. The strip becomes a literal dawn-to-dusk gradient made of your own choices, with carried props marked along it. One line of copy above it is enough: 'harimu, dari subuh ke malam'. Then put the same strip as a single full-width row on the 1080x1920 share canvas beneath the archetype name, and draw the carried props on the result mascot too.
ideas.why: It closes the journey loop with an image instead of another paragraph — you see your whole day at a glance, which is the strongest possible reply to 'ceritanya patah banget'. It also means two friends who land on the same archetype get visibly different cards, which is worth more for sharing than any copy tweak. And it needs no new art at all: it reuses the answer tiles from the sticker-grid idea at small scale, so the cost is layout, not illustration.

ideas.title: Pintu yang Belum Kebuka — replay engine built on the 4 doors
ideas.what: On the result screen, under the archetype, render an inline-SVG "peta hari ini": your 5 scenes as pastel thumbnails joined by a dotted trail in your archetype color — and at the trail's start, the 3 doors you did NOT open, drawn closed, dimmed, gently wobbling (@keyframes ketuk) with a soft knock sound on tap. Each carries a one-line tease, no paragraph: "Pintu 🎨 — ada meja penuh alat yang masih nungguin kamu." Tapping one calls startFrom(doorKey): Babak 1 is pre-answered, so the replay opens straight into Scene 2B. A new story is 4 taps, not 14. Persist opened doors in localStorage (emina_doors) and show a 4-glyph "paspor" strip (2/4 kebuka) on intro and result. Opening all 4 unlocks a real 7th card — "Si Pembuka Semua Pintu", gold-on-pastel, #MadeToExplore — with its own share card frame. Attach to index.html: new #map block in #result, SCENES/sceneSVG reused for thumbnails, reset() gains a startDoor param.
ideas.why: Branching is worthless if nobody sees a second branch. This converts the user's new 4-door Babak 1 into the replay loop: short re-entry (4 taps), visible incompleteness (3 wobbling doors = an itch), a collectible counter, and a genuinely earned secret ending that is worth screenshotting precisely because it cannot be gotten in one run. It also makes "kirim ke 3 bestie" natural — each friend takes a different door and they compare.

ideas.title: Kartu "1 dari 576" — every share card is visibly a different story
ideas.what: Encode the run as a 5-char path code: door letter (A–D) + option index per babak, base36'd → e.g. A3K2F. Print it small at the card's bottom edge with an honest computed stat: "jalan cerita A3K2F · 1 dari 576" (4 doors × 3 × 3 × 4 × 4 = 576 — real math, no invented player counts). Above the CTA footer, draw a "journey strip": the 5 scene illustrations you actually walked, as 96px circular thumbnails on a dotted line, rasterized through the existing data-URI SVG trick in loadMascotImg(). Also write the code to location.hash (#p=A3K2F) and include it in copyLink. A visit with #p= shows a pre-intro card before #intro: "Temenmu ngajak kamu jalanin cerita dia 👀" with two buttons — "Ikutin jalannya" (auto-steps the same route, beats and all) or "Aku bikin sendiri".
ideas.why: Right now two Spotlight Creators post an identical image, so the second one does not bother. A visible route plus a code means her card is hers, and friends ask "kok jalanmu beda?" — which is the comment that pulls them in. "1 dari 576" is a flex that is also true, and the #p= link turns a screenshot into a playable invitation instead of a dead image.

ideas.title: Duel Bestie — a second share card that requires a friend's code
ideas.what: On the result screen: "Duel sama bestie 👯". Paste her 5-char code (or arrive via #duel=CODE) and decode it client-side into her answers → her archetype and her 4 trait poles, no backend needed. Render a second 1080×1920 card: two mascots facing each other, background split-gradient of both archetype colors, the 4 trait tracks drawn once with two knobs (✨ kamu vs 💫 dia), a chemistry score computed as 100 minus normalized L1 distance across the four axes, and one verdict line from a hand-written pair matrix (21 pairs + 6 twins = 27 short lines), e.g. "Si Bos Muda × Si Jari Ajaib — kamu yang mimpin, dia yang bikin cantik. Bahaya kalau kolab 🔥". Add one shared-choice line: "Di Babak 4 kalian milih hal yang sama 🫶". Reuse buildCard's canvas with a layout flag so only one draw path exists.
ideas.why: Self-expression cards are posted; comparison cards are sent. To get a duel she has to DM a friend and ask for her code, so the outbound message is the mechanic rather than an afterthought — and the friend must take the quiz to answer. The twin case ("kita sama persis??") and the low-match case are both screenshot-worthy, so there is no boring outcome.

ideas.title: Cermin Senja — a reveal the user performs with her finger
ideas.what: Replace the 2.65s LOAD_LINES spinner with three beats. (1) The 5 scene illustrations she actually saw fly in and stack into a deck (CSS transforms, ~1.2s). (2) The deck flips into a frosted pane: her mascot behind blur(14px), nickname masked as ████, tagline hidden. (3) "Usap buat liat 👆" — an overlay canvas sized to the hero card, filled with a pastel frost, erased by pointermove with globalCompositeOperation='destination-out' and a soft 70px brush. Track cleared pixels; at ~55% it auto-completes, the frost fades, confetti fires and the result lands. Fallbacks: a plain "Buka ✨" button for no-pointer, reduced-motion, or 6s timeout. Keep every word on this screen to four or fewer.
ideas.why: The current reveal is something that happens to her; this is something she does, which is the difference between a screenshot and a screen recording. Blurred-then-wiped is natively a video — her own hand in frame — and that clip is the most shareable asset the quiz can produce. The forced tap also guarantees the result screen is actually looked at instead of scrolled past.

ideas.title: Caption kit + tag slots + dual aspect — closing the gap between wanting to post and posting
ideas.what: Four concrete additions to the share modal. (a) "Salin caption" with a per-archetype pre-written line so she never has to be clever: "aku si Anak FYP 💄 ternyata versi masa depanku ada di depan kamera. kalian tipe apa? [link] @eminacosmetics #Emina20Under20" plus her path code. (b) Aspect chips "Story 9:16 / Feed 1:1" rebuilding from one draw function with a layout param (the 1:1 drops the journey strip, keeps nickname + mascot + CTA). (c) On the card itself, "tag 3 bestie kamu 👇" above three dotted rounded slots — empty name plates read as an instruction and people literally tag over them in the IG editor. (d) iOS coach: when navigator.canShare({files}) is false, animate a finger glyph over the #cardImg with "Tekan lama gambarnya → Save to Photos" instead of silently falling through to a download that does nothing on Safari.
ideas.why: Every other idea leaks out through this screen. Writing a caption is the step where enthusiasm dies, so pre-write it. Three blank tag slots turn one post into three invitations with no new UI. The Safari long-press coach is the difference between a share flow that works for roughly everyone and one that silently fails for most iPhone users — which is most of this audience.

ideas.title: Lemari Stiker — and sticker #7 only opens at the real registration
ideas.what: Give each archetype a die-cut sticker (inline SVG: white outline, pastel fill, slight tilt, soft shadow). On result, hers pops in: "Stiker kamu kebuka — 1/6". A "Lemari Stiker" screen shows all six, locked ones as pastel silhouettes with hidden nicknames; replays through unopened doors fill the shelf. The seventh slot is gold: "20 UNDER 20", and it cannot be unlocked by playing. Tapping it opens bit.ly/Emina20Under20 in a new tab; on return the app asks "Udah daftar? ✦ Buka stiker emas" and, on her say-so, unlocks a gold frame plus a small 20U20 badge drawn into every future share card. Keep the framing honest and warm — "kita percaya kamu 💛" — and never claim it was verified.
ideas.why: The registration button is currently a dead end at the bottom of the page, competing with the share button it will always lose to. As the last empty slot in a collection she is already filling, the click becomes progression. Better: the gold frame makes registering visible inside shared images, so her friends see the badge and the campaign markets itself through the card instead of through a CTA nobody taps.

ideas.title: Suara Empat Pintu — door ambience that becomes her 5-note signature
ideas.what: WebAudio only, no files. Four door motifs: Sorot = band-passed noise crowd murmur + 3 rising notes + shutter click; Karya = short noise snips (scissors) + marimba-ish triangle tones; Hati = two low thumps (knock) + filtered-noise rain + a warm two-note; Jelajah = lowpass-swept wind + a fast pitch-glide chirp + an open fifth. Every later choice appends one note to melody[], so the run composes a 5-note "melodi hari ini" that plays under the Cermin Senja reveal. On the result, show it as five pastel bars with "Putar lagi 🔊" and one line: "Ini suara hari kamu." Gate it properly: intro offers "nyalain suara 🔊 / nanti aja" (autoplay policy needs the gesture), a persistent mute toggle top-right, state in localStorage, and everything silent by default if she declines.
ideas.why: The brief asks for sound and atmosphere per door; this makes it do double duty. Stories get recorded with sound on, and a composed motif is what makes a 4-second clip feel produced rather than like a screen capture of a web page. It also does the heavy lifting the removed text used to do: a crowd murmur behind a door says "this is a place" faster and cheaper than two sentences of narration.
